correctness.rationale: A complete proof counts 21-3k+e(S) edges remaining after deleting k cubic-graph vertices, forcing k>=4 and independence at k=4. It examines all five bipartition-count cases: (4,0),(3,1), their duals, and rejects (2,2) by an explicit retained 8-cycle formed by two distinct perfect matchings on four Fano points. The surviving configurations are precisely the four-subsets of fourteen geometrically defined five-sets, distinct families intersecting in at most two graph vertices; this forces 14 disjoint K5 exchange components, 70 optima and 140 exchange edges. Both supplied standalone checkers, from orthogonal-vector and cyclic difference-set models, independently enumerated all subsets through cardinality four and independently reproduced all counts and classification. A checker additionally exhaustively verifies 3-vertex-connectivity. This is a finite theorem with complete proof; no extrapolation.

originality.rationale: No equivalent or stronger Heawood four-FVS configuration and exchange classification was identified in actual published-finding corpus searches, accessible historical claims, or the relevant primary indexed literature. Bousquet et al. study the same FVS exchange rule and give disconnected 3-connected cubic examples at odd FVS sizes at least five, but their displayed assertions do not imply the precise even-size-four Heawood structure. The foundational geometry and graph count are credited. Residual risk: neither relevant publisher full text nor all unindexed computational tables was inspectable, so priority clearance is not claimed.
residual_risks: The 2023 feedback-vertex-set reconfiguration journal full text was inaccessible after bounded OA/preprint and authorized institutional attempts; an undisplayed appendix could cover the graph.
The full 2022 cubic decycling article was inaccessible, so its abstract does not rule out details elsewhere in its body.
Unindexed graph tables, preprints, and alternate Levi/Fano graph names may contain the same classification; search absence is not a priority certificate.

value.rationale: The problem classifies all optimal FVS configurations and connected components under a standard one-vertex reconfiguration operation on the Heawood incidence graph, a natural 3-connected bipartite cubic cage. The 14K5 geometry provides a structural invariant built from the Fano point-line duality, explains disconnectedness without a trivial isolated solution, and gives a small even k=4 complement to earlier odd-k disconnected constructions. Exact count 70 and component K5 structure are natural full classifications, not arbitrary slices or mere code output.
